key_finding: In vitro assay establishing phytoene synthase activity; basis of the IDA GO:0046905 and GO:0016117 annotations. No fractionation or localisation reported.
confidence_and_limitations: High for activity, silent on location

claim_tested: CrtB presents an amphipathic or hydrophobic membrane-docking surface
key_finding: Largest apolar patch 503 A2 is interior (centroid 12.4 A from protein centre vs 18.2 A mean); a 5 A probe removes 72% of it, leaving 142 A2 of true outer apolar surface, below the cytosolic control mean 159 +/- 39 A2 (z = -0.43) and far below monotopic PGHS-1 at 264 A2 (z = +2.71).
context: AlphaFold monomer model, mean pLDDT 94.2, 309 aa; 23-structure benchmark panel
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high; model not experimental, dimer interface not modelled

claim_tested: Surface amphipathic helices with high hydrophobic moment exist
key_finding: 0 of 12 P-SEA-assigned helices reach the amphipathic threshold muH > 0.50. Maximum muH 0.453 over a 9-residue helix (18-26); the longest candidate helix 208-231 gives muH 0.394.
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high; moment analysis is sequence-and-geometry based

claim_tested: The hydrophobic patch is conserved because it docks membrane
key_finding: Patch residues are more conserved than the rest of the protein (mean identity 0.629 vs 0.412, Mann-Whitney p = 4.0e-4, 147 bacterial CrtB orthologues), but the patch is the geranylgeranyl-binding channel, so conservation tracks catalysis.
confidence_and_limitations: Medium-high; conservation alone cannot distinguish the two explanations

claim_tested: Bacterial family members have a known membrane-docking surface
key_finding: S. aureus CrtM, the closest bacterial structural homologue, has an outer apolar patch of 120 A2, inside the cytosolic range. OPM contains human squalene synthase 1EZF at a shallow dG of -5.1 kcal/mol but has no CrtM and no phytoene synthase entry.
context: S. aureus CrtM crystal structure; OPM curated set
confidence_and_limitations: High for the absence of an OPM entry

claim_tested: The phytoene synthase module is membrane-associated
key_finding: In the Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous CrtYB fusion, the phytoene synthase domain fractionates as a soluble 40 kDa protein while the lycopene cyclase domain of the same polypeptide is in the membrane fraction.
confidence_and_limitations: High; the cleanest internal control in the family

key_finding: The phytoene-synthase complex in etioplasts and etiochloroplasts is soluble in the stroma, while the downstream dehydrogenase, cis-trans isomerase and cyclase are membrane-bound.
Narcissus PSY is localised at thylakoid membranes in mature chloroplasts, so plant PSY membrane association is real but developmental-stage dependent.
confidence_and_limitations: High for plants; does not transfer to bacteria

claim_tested: A membrane CC term for bacterial CrtB has database precedent
key_finding: 500/500 bacterial CrtB entries, including all 14 Swiss-Prot reviewed ones, carry no subcellular location comment and no GO CC term; 1/500 has a TRANSMEM feature. Same family elsewhere: plants 30/32, fungi 33/34, metazoa 10/10 annotated.

8 annotations, 0 cellular component. Experimental: GO:0046905 and GO:0016117 (both IDA, PMID:9593819). Electronic transfers that conflict with the demonstrated activity: GO:0004311 GGPP synthase activity and GO:0051996 squalene synthase [NAD(P)H] activity, both IEA GO_REF:0000002 from InterPro.
